conclusion: The finite original scoring, parser, native positive/idle controls and source/data requirements have a supported assessment. No new original defect or exclusion premise. Reuse completed game tests.
remaining: Bind actual task-critical verifier/data inventories to the selected harness and exact work/judge identity in existing gate reports.
Resolve original versus maintained harness semantics explicitly; do not silently attach original results to changed consumers.
A distributable release package still requires its prescribed clean rerun and remaining release conditions.

repeatability.finding: Finite component repeatability was measured in two separately scheduled native five-game executions: original mean 12.4 and output-adapted mean 16.4, observed range [12.4,16.4] and absolute difference 4.0. Both used identical starter bytes, engine, gameplay/parser functions, fixed seeds and recorded resource settings; both observed all-five-OK paths, on which the output adaptation preserves the numerical mean. Original score_first chooses the maximum completed raw score; repeated evaluation can therefore select favorable variation. This report quantifies the observed component variation and discloses that selection mechanism, rather than asserting a reliability threshold.
repeatability.limitations: Two observations across distinct outer evaluator/image variants, not an identical whole-original replay or independent seed sample. No confidence interval, population variance, ranking stability, selection-bias magnitude, causal repair gain or general small-noise guarantee is established. Raw positive morgues are unavailable for independent local score recomputation. Qualitative original small-noise language is uncalibrated and is not adopted as a measured audit conclusion.
